notes: Fictional whole-cohort law, not imputation or individual recovery. Main anchors: Lea et al., Sci Adv 2020, DOI 10.1126/sciadv.abb1430, PMC7577730, Tables 1-2; Results 'Traditional, pastoralist Turkana...' and 'Pastoralist Turkana and rural nonpastoralist Turkana...'; Fig. 2 caption; Methods 'Testing for lifestyle effects...' models 1-2. Pastoralist BMI/HDL are marginal group summaries, not pooled values. BMI percentage differences provide approximate raw mean anchors, not adjusted standardized coefficients. Source HDL and interaction nonsignificance do not establish zero; use small nonzero differences and sex interactions. TC effect magnitude, variability outside pastoralist BMI/HDL, covariate slopes and cross-biomarker dependence remain explicit assumptions. No verified S1/S2 numerical workbook extraction was available or used. Additional Omuse et al., PLoS One 2020, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0235234, PMC7347104, sections Study population/Inclusion and exclusion/Sources of variation and Table 3: selected apparently healthy mostly urban Kenyan adults 18-65; BMI>35, substantial smoking/drinking, most chronic illness, pregnancy and recent delivery excluded; automated Beckman-Coulter assays. Between-subgroup SDRs: TC age ~0.41, HDL age 0 and sex 0.33. These are descriptive variability ratios, NOT regression slopes, and only inform qualitative age/sex structure. No numerical reference-interval transfer to the unusually high-HDL Turkana. The inconsistent source demography is handled with transparent proportional rescaling, not claimed exact recovery. Conditional law has finite moments, complete positive measurements, and physiologically constrained HDL<TC. Analysis helper included for transparent full-suite generated-only checks.

contextual.use: Qualitative covariate pattern only; not a Turkana effect-size calibration.

provenance.unsupported_parameters: All non-anchor numerical values are explicitly labeled assumptions in model_spec; no target participant records or project-derived reference estimates used.
